parsed.explanation: Thin-data jurisdiction resolving toward structural risk. De facto criminalisation via 'good morals' provisions usable against visible gender-nonconforming conduct, no legal gender recognition, no SOGI anti-discrimination law, LGBTI organisations barred from registering, and pervasive documented social/religious intolerance with taboo and shunning. No documented arrests, raids or violence against trans people — but the record is explicitly sparse, so silence is not safety (rule 13). Recourse (police, human-rights commission) is unproven. Extrapolated signals: morality statutes treated as live prosecutorial tools, zero institutional acceptance, weak protection framework. This sits between documented-enforcement regimes (0.25) and unbounded-but-better-institutionalised ambiguity (0.45); no evidence supports Reduced Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: No LGR domestically; foreign documents assessed against a framework offering no recognition equivalent. Whether amended foreign markers affect entry/visa/airport processing is unresolved.
entry_documents.interaction: Document presentation may interact with 'good morals' scrutiny if appearance/marker mismatch draws official attention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Authorities retain power to prosecute public same-sex conduct under Sections 353/354; scope undefined by any case law. Baseline prisons described as harsh (2015, general).
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visible trans visitor could be swept into morality-provision investigation with unbounded outcome; custody conditions generally poor.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No legal remedy for refusal of service, housing or facility entry on SOGI grounds; no discrimination prohibition beyond employment.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Service or facility refusal would leave the traveller without recourse.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Status and conduct treated as taboo; pervasive social and religious intolerance (2023); no public societal discussion tolerated. Morality provisions are the prosecutorial instrument.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Complaints can be filed with police or the national human-rights commission — documented route, unproven effectiveness.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State is a bystander rather than documented perpetrator; but no institutional acceptance signals exist.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No dated incidents of violence against trans people citable; 2023 report cites no official violence cases. Societal discrimination pattern documented, not state action.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Police complaint channel exists; effectiveness undocumented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of recorded incidents in a scarce-data country is a sourcing gap, not evidence of safety.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No SOGI discrimination law; no case law bounding Sections 353/354; no trans-specific incident or prevalence data with denominators; no domestic advocacy bodies (registration barred).
remedies_unknowns.protection: National human-rights commission and police complaints channels documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Documentation gap 2009–present means unknowns cannot be resolved toward safety.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A documents a universal, routinely enforced visitor-facing exclusion regime. Here enforcement against trans visitors is not documented, but the structural intolerance and usable morality statutes are comparably hostile with far less certainty — slightly below that anchor's documented consistency.

0.55-B has administrative-only consequences, working (if slow) appeal desks and functioning institutions. This jurisdiction lacks any proven remedy, has de facto criminalisation and unbounded statute scope — clearly lower.

0.25-D documents selective police application, entrapment and blackmail with documented convictions. This dossier documents no enforcement incidents, only latent prosecutorial power and pervasive intolerance — slightly above 0.25-D on documented practice, but thin data limits confidence.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines latent morality statutes treated as prosecutorial tools, zero gender recognition, no SOGI protections, barred advocacy organisations, and documented pervasive intolerance — with no documented enforcement incidents against trans people, but also no documented safety: the record is explicitly sparse and every unknown resolves toward the structural risk the legal framework implies. The traveller's main exposures are unbounded 'good morals' prosecution risk if visible or publicly outed, and service/facility refusal with no remedy. Recourse channels exist on paper only. This is High Risk: above documented-punishment jurisdictions, well below any jurisdiction with working protections.
